text: I'm calling about the health insurance enquiry you submitted last week. Is this a good time?

text: I should mention I have diabetes, type two, diagnosed three years ago.
why: Arms the waiting-period disclosure requirement but is not itself a signal.

speaker: agent
text: That's absolutely fine, diabetes is very common and we cover it.
why: REQUIRED: agent answered a pre-existing condition question without disclosing the waiting period. This is the brief's 'skipped disclosure' case.

speaker: customer
text: Okay good. My wife also needs cover, she's not insured at all right now.
why: REQUIRED: explicit second-life opportunity. The brief's 'missed cross-sell' case.

speaker: agent
text: Right, noted. So for your own policy, the premium works out to about eighteen thousand rupees a year.
why: Quotes a figure without saying it is indicative or subject to underwriting. Also ignores the cross-sell just offered.

speaker: customer

text: Sorry, the line is a bit bad. Could you say that again?
why: NOISE CASE: audio trouble, not frustration. A naive sentiment detector fires here; it must not.

speaker: customer
text: No, I don't have a second car, it's just the one.
why: NOISE CASE: negated cross-sell. The phrase 'second car' appears but the answer is no. Must not fire.

speaker: customer
text: And I'm not frustrated, I just want to understand the numbers.

speaker: customer
text: Although honestly, this is the third time I've called about this and nobody has given me a straight answer.

speaker: agent
text: I understand. Let me just reassure you, your claim will definitely be approved, there's nothing to worry about.
why: REQUIRED: agent guarantees a claim outcome. Compliance exposure, and the hardest case because the surrounding tone is reassuring.
